claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old and lives with you.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't signed up for anything yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in paid work? If so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

Since Alex is 18 years old, not in approved education or training, and not working, I need to clarify one final point:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** (If he left education or training at 16 or 17 and registered with these services, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks, but since he's now 18, this may not apply.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just finished school and hasn't done anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Child Benefit normally covers children under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you can still qualify if they are under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training. Since Alex is 18 and is not currently in any approved education or training program, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria.

**However**, if Alex's situation changes in the future - for example, if he:
- Enrolls in approved education or training (such as college, sixth form, or an approved training course)
- He would then qualify again until he turns 20

If Alex does decide to pursue education or training in the future, you would be able to make a new claim for Child Benefit at that time.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

Additionally, the 20-week extension that applies when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services does not apply, as Alex has not registered with either. Furthermore, Alex is not working 24 hours or more per week, which would also disqualify him. Since Alex is 18, not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or armed forces, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.
